evaluation_limitations: The supplied RAG output includes one claimed retrieved passage, but no independent retrieval log or corpus artifact is available to verify corpus fidelity.
Primary detection and classification scores are therefore based on the raw interview, generation specification, frozen segment map, and RAG output only.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Honestly, once I laid the twenty-one and twenty-three side by side, it wasn't close. ... the contrast between the other two was just so stark that it became the frame I was working from.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant lets the near-priced inferior full-service option frame the choice of Vendor C and does not independently assess whether Vendor A meets the three-flow scope.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I went with Candidate X. ... if he could deliver that caliber of interaction design there, I figured he'd bring the same rigor to documenting decisions and communicating with stakeholders here. ... I looked at the visual work and sort of assumed the rest would follow.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant generalizes prestige and visual polish to unverified documentation and communication abilities, despite Candidate Y's directly relevant process evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The activation numbers on the dashboard ticked up right after. I took it as a sign the adjustments were working. ... I heard that, but the timing felt too clean to ignore. It really did look like my changes were the driver.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant attributes an underpowered, confounded uptick to their own manual rule changes and acts on that attribution despite the Data lead's warning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The uptick partly reversed once the email campaign ended, and she noted the causal driver was still unconfirmed. So it's genuinely unclear how much of that first bump was actually the rule changes.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a later uncertainty update that acknowledges reversal and unresolved causality; it contains no hidden manifested bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I pushed to keep customizing the legacy component rather than migrate. We'd already put three sprints into it — restarting felt like throwing that away ... The one-sprint number was probably a better bet purely on cost and risk.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Past effort is used to justify continuation even though the forward-looking one-sprint migration estimate is better on cost and risk and resolves known defects.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Selection of the target vendor option is driven by favorable contrast against a similarly priced but inferior intermediate option, rather than independent assessment of the cheapest sufficient option.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The RAG label exactly matches the hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG identifies the three-option contrast, the near-priced inferior middle option, and the displacement of the cheaper sufficient option.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited participant quotations are present in the raw interview and support the decision rationale without relying on hindsight.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A single salient positive attribute (portfolio brand prestige) is used to infer unrelated positive qualities (documentation rigor, communication skill) without direct supporting evidence.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The RAG label exactly matches the hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG captures the spread from recognizable-company prestige and visual polish to unverified documentation and communication competence.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited participant quotations are present in the raw interview and directly support the inference and lack of verification.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Overattribution of an observed metric change to the designer's own specific manual action, despite acknowledged insufficient statistical power and unresolved confounding factors.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a related neighboring construct, but it is not an approved equivalent of Illusion of control. The RAG's label emphasizes selective interpretation of evidence, while the hidden target emphasizes overattributing an outcome to one's own action.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Despite the label mismatch, the RAG explicitly captures self-attribution of the uptick, disregard of the sample-size and marketing-email confounds, and action on that causal attribution; this is a full match to the hidden mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited participant quotations are present in the raw interview and support both the self-attribution and the acknowledged methodological warnings.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Continuation of a design approach is justified primarily by the magnitude of prior invested effort rather than a forward-looking comparison of remaining costs and benefits.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Sunk cost fallacy is an established scholarly equivalent for the benchmark's Sunk Cost Bias label, and the stated mechanism matches fully.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG identifies prior three-sprint investment as the reason to continue despite a better forward-looking migration cost/risk comparison.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited participant quotations are present in the raw interview and include the counterfactual that isolates the sunk-cost influence.

overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: 3/4 hidden instances matched under the strict scorecard at every threshold; precision, recall, and F1 are 0.7500.

main_failure_modes: The rules-engine finding was assigned the near-neighbor label Confirmation bias instead of the hidden target Illusion of control, causing one strict label error despite full mechanism coverage.
Corpus support for three findings was explicitly unavailable, and the one claimed citation cannot be independently verified from the supplied inputs.
main_strengths: All four findings were localized to the correct positive reasoning segments with valid interview quotations.
The RAG captured the defining mechanisms for all four hidden instances, including the underpowered and confounded causal attribution.
The RAG avoided adding a false positive to the negative post-test uncertainty segment.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has perfect segment-level detection and mechanism-first instance performance, but strict label-plus-mechanism performance is reduced by one taxonomy substitution: Confirmation bias for Illusion of control. Confidence expansion and candidate inclusion have no effect because every finding is high confidence and candidate_biases is empty.
